subject: Canonical club key
decision: every table keys on the schedule abbreviation (ARI, LA, WAS) and the alias used by the injury and standings pages is recorded as data
why: one key across eleven tables is what makes a join safe; the mismatch raised a real KeyError in the first run of the model, which is how it was found
alternative_rejected: keeping AZ in the standings table and mapping at read time, which would have made the alias invisible to a reviewer
cost_of_being_wrong: a wrong join silently corrupts a count; a recorded alias corrupts nothing

subject: Margin damping in the published line
decision: published lines stay undamped (lambda = 1.00); every fit is published as analysis
why: the grid search returns 0.0 at the Week 7 vintage, 0.8 at Week 8 and 1.0 at Week 9 on 14-44 games; baking an unstable in-sample fit into the line would make the line incomparable across strategies
alternative_rejected: publishing the fitted lambda as the model's number, which would let the board score a fitted shrink as if it were a rule
cost_of_being_wrong: none for accuracy; the fit is still useful to a reader, which is why it is published

subject: How the leaderboard ranks signal
decision: Brier skill against each target event's own base rate, then points of absolute error saved versus a naive line, then sample size
why: raw Brier is not comparable between a cover event and a favourite-win event: the moneyline row looks excellent (0.192) only because its event hits 73% of the time, and its skill score is +0.018
alternative_rejected: ranking on raw Brier or on units, both of which reward structure or variance rather than accuracy
cost_of_being_wrong: a ranking a reader cannot interpret; the base rate and the interval are published beside every score

subject: Opening numbers for Week 10 markets
decision: the prior session's published CSV, at its merge commit, is used as the opening number and labelled prior_session_publication
why: it is the only earlier publication of these fourteen markets in the repository, and its own commit hash makes it citable
alternative_rejected: silently treating today's single row as both open and close, or leaving the opening column empty and losing the movement that does exist
cost_of_being_wrong: movement mixes two model versions, so the row carries flag D966-F02 and the movement strategy is blocked until two snapshots share a version

subject: Depth, where no depth chart exists
decision: a designation count is published as a hard lower bound, and only a headline naming the replacement counts as evidence of the tier
why: the report ranks nobody; an inferred depth chart would be the invention the brief forbids, while a floor is arithmetic on what is printed
alternative_rejected: estimating second/third/fourth string from roster order or contract year, which no official page here supports
cost_of_being_wrong: understating depth rather than overstating it - which is the direction a reviewer should prefer

subject: Blank cells
decision: a value is blank when no citable source supplies it; the row still publishes, with a status string and a flag id, and a placeholder token is a verifier error
why: n/a, TBD and - are read as data by the next person, and a filled cell cannot be distinguished from a fabricated one afterwards
alternative_rejected: filling the market and moneyline columns with an assumed price or a 0.5 probability
cost_of_being_wrong: the pack publishes fewer numbers and every one of them is traceable

subject: Rewards
decision: standing, compute priority and a badge; no money
why: the rights position limits league data to non-commercial use, and a cash prize on betting outcomes would aim an autonomous board at profit instead of accuracy
alternative_rejected: a nominal cash tier for the top strategy

subject: Gate ordering versus publication
decision: the gate runs in the same pass and every failing strategy is still published, labelled paper
why: refusing to publish a failing row would hide the reason it failed, which is the opposite of what the flag register is for
alternative_rejected: suppressing non-qualifying strategies from the board entirely (suggestion D966-S09, not applied)
cost_of_being_wrong: a strategy appears for one run before it can be demoted; the transition table records it

subject: Probabilities that need data the feed lacks
decision: for scoring only, the earliest measurable dispersion vintage is substituted and every leg using it is labelled substituted_forward_from_vintage_7
why: dropping Weeks 7-8 from the calibration statistics would shrink the sample to hide the gap; peeking without saying so would be worse than peeking
alternative_rejected: silently reusing the Week 9 sigma for every game
cost_of_being_wrong: a slightly optimistic calibration figure at the early vintages, disclosed column by column

subject: Scope of the results feed
decision: Weeks 7-10 only, with the boundary stated on every table and a self-serveable backfill path
why: reading more weeks is cheap but was outside this session's window; publishing n honestly is what keeps the smaller window usable
alternative_rejected: quietly quoting season-long correlations off a four-week feed
cost_of_being_wrong: wide intervals and a small-sample flag on every coefficient - the correct cost
